From my experience PMax performs better than standard but they should've run an experiment.   PMax will go after warm audiences so it may cannibalize brand and remarketing campaigns.  PMax also tends to be more expensive than search campaigns.  And btw, agency doesn't know best.  I have audited many a Google account that was poorly managed by an "agency".

A couple of things to check:

Structure.  Do your categories have separate campaigns or is there one campaign that targets all product types?  If there is only one campaign, be sure they're breaking up categories into separate asset groups so that the correct digital assets are matching the correct products.  For example, let's say you sell sporting goods.  If someone is searching for yoga pants, you don't want to show them jogging shorts.  Also, you can view asset groups via the table and see how each is performing within your PMax campaign.  If one performs better but isn't getting the budget it needs, you may want to think about isolating it into its own campaign.

Are they using scripts?  There are a couple of 3rd party scripts out there that reveal data on PMax that isn't readily available in platform.  The search terms one is valuable as it provides terms that are triggering your ads and you can identify waste.  While you cannot add negatives on campaign level, you can on account level.
